description_good_justification: README describes dbackup-mcp as a typed MCP server for curated DBackup backup administration, its supported surface, boundaries, configuration, permissions, security model, compatibility, development, and release lifecycle. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: README documents installation and use; GitHub Issues accept feedback; CONTRIBUTING.md documents contributions. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/README.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the public contribution workflow, private security-reporting route, tests, documentation expectations, dependency changes, and changelog requirements. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the Python 3.12/uv baseline, repository verification command, test requirements, bounded MCP/security expectations, documentation updates, and dependency-change boundaries. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_justification: The project is released under the MIT license. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open-source license.
license_location_justification: The full license text is in LICENSE at the repository root. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics_justification: README documents purpose, supported workflows, requirements, configuration, source execution, permissions, security, compatibility, verification, release behavior, and license. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/README.md
documentation_interface_justification: README summarizes the curated MCP surface and links to docs/tools.md, which documents every tool, mutation classification, permissions, guards, and externally visible inputs/outputs. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/docs/tools.md
sites_https_justification: The project repository, issue tracker, releases, and source distribution are served over HTTPS by GitHub.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests provide public, searchable, URL-addressable project discussion. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/issues
english_justification: The public source documentation, contribution policy, security policy, changelog, code comments, and commit messages are maintained in English.
maintained_justification: The repository is actively maintained with current commits, CI/security hardening, dependency maintenance, and an accepted v0.1.0 release. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/commits/main
repo_public_justification: The complete source repository is public. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp
repo_track_justification: git tracks source changes and public history on GitHub.
repo_interim_justification: Interim changes are published as commits and pull requests on the public repository between releases.
repo_distributed_justification: git is a distributed version-control system.
version_unique_justification: The maintained release has a unique SemVer version, git tag, GitHub Release, and immutable release assets. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/releases
version_semver_justification: Published releases use strict vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH Semantic Versioning tags and the release workflow validates tag/source/package version parity. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
version_tags_justification: Published releases use matching vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH git tags. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/tags
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md records user-visible release changes and the repository release workflow publishes versioned GitHub Release notes/assets. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: There are no publicly known dbackup-mcp vulnerabilities that need identification in release notes.
report_process_justification: Bug reports and feature proposals are accepted through GitHub Issues and documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is the public issue tracker. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/issues
report_responses_justification: The young project has no eligible long-standing unanswered bug reports; the public issue process is active. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/issues
enhancement_responses_justification: The young project has no eligible long-standing unanswered enhancement requests; the public issue process is active. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/issues
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public searchable archive with stable issue URLs. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md instructs reporters to use GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting, forbids public secret disclosure, and states what a useful report should contain. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports use GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting as documented in SECURITY.md. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received during the project's lifetime, so there is no report-response sample to measure.
build_justification: scripts/verify.sh creates the locked environment, compiles Python sources/tests, runs pytest, builds wheel and source distribution, and verifies both artifacts exist. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/scripts/verify.sh
build_common_tools_justification: The documented build uses standard Python 3.12, uv, pytest, and Python packaging tooling. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
build_floss_tools_justification: The build and test path uses open-source Python, uv, pytest, and standard Python packaging tooling.
test_justification: The repository contains an automated pytest suite and repository verification runs it from the locked environment. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/tree/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: ./scripts/verify.sh is the documented repository verification entry point and invokes pytest after compile validation. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/scripts/verify.sh
test_most_justification: The project does not currently publish branch-coverage evidence demonstrating that most branches, inputs, and functionality meet the suggested coverage criterion.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions CI runs the repository verification path on proposed changes and main. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires new behavior and bug fixes to add or update automated tests where a regression test is practical. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: The maintained repository contains regression and contract tests covering the bounded MCP surface and DBackup compatibility behavior. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/tree/main/tests
tests_documented_added_justification: The mandatory test expectation is public in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: The authored implementation is interpreted Python rather than a warning-configurable compiled language; repository verification uses compileall and tests as fail-closed syntax/runtime gates.
warnings_fixed_justification: There is no compiler-warning stream for the authored Python code; compile or test failures fail repository verification and CI.
warnings_strict_justification: Compiler warning-level flags do not apply to the authored Python implementation.
know_secure_design_justification: Primary maintainer Ronald de Wit has self-certified knowledge of basic secure software design principles; project-specific application is documented in docs/SECURE-DEVELOPMENT.md.
know_common_errors_justification: Primary maintainer Ronald de Wit has self-certified knowledge of common security errors relevant to the implementation stack; project-specific classes and mitigations are documented in docs/SECURE-DEVELOPMENT.md.
crypto_published_justification: dbackup-mcp does not implement or define a cryptographic algorithm or protocol.
crypto_call_justification: The runtime does not implement an application cryptographic protocol; HTTPS and release attestations are supplied by external platform/library boundaries.
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptographic algorithm is implemented by dbackup-mcp.
crypto_keylength_justification: dbackup-mcp does not manage cryptographic keys or choose cryptographic key lengths.
crypto_working_justification: dbackup-mcp does not implement an application cryptographic algorithm or protocol.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: dbackup-mcp does not select or implement application cryptographic algorithms.
crypto_pfs_justification: dbackup-mcp does not terminate or configure TLS.
crypto_password_storage_justification: dbackup-mcp does not implement user accounts or password storage.
crypto_random_justification: dbackup-mcp does not generate cryptographic keys, passwords, or session secrets.
delivery_mitm_justification: Source and release distribution use HTTPS through GitHub, and release artifacts include SHA256SUMS plus signed GitHub/Sigstore provenance for future releases. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: Release downloads are HTTPS-delivered; the release workflow publishes SHA256SUMS and a Sigstore attestation bundle for future releases. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched project vulnerabilities of medium or higher severity; dependency/security review is part of maintained release acceptance. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known unresolved critical dbackup-mcp vulnerabilities or critical dependency advisories.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: GitHub Secret Scanning and Push Protection are enabled, production credentials are excluded from public CI, and the project explicitly forbids secrets in issues, tests, logs, or commits. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
static_analysis_justification: GitHub CodeQL analyzes the Python source and GitHub Actions workflow code for the maintained repository. https://github.com/X1pheR/dbackup-mcp/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL covers common vulnerability classes for Python and workflow code.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Current maintained CodeQL analyses are green; repository CI must pass before accepted main changes.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs continuously on maintained repository changes through GitHub's configured code-scanning setup.
dynamic_analysis_justification: The project does not currently run a fuzzer/property-based dynamic-analysis tool or publish at least 80% branch coverage, so it does not claim this suggested criterion.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The authored project code is Python rather than a memory-unsafe language such as C or C++.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Tests use ordinary assertions, but the project does not claim a dedicated dynamic-analysis configuration that intentionally enables widespread assertions.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The project is not currently claiming dynamic-analysis coverage under the Best Practices definition, so no vulnerabilities have been discovered through such a tool.
